title: Publish Q1 2026 internal perf baseline report (tables + takeaways + release gating policy)
creator: Talia Benson
dependencies: PM-931 (self) requires baseline freeze confirmation from eng-runtime
description:
## Context
We’ve completed the bulk of the Q1 2026 “Perf baseline & representative workload suite” implementation (harness + workloads + dashboards + canary wiring). We now need a packaged, internal-only baseline report that is readable by:
- Execs (Infra/Reliability + Applied ML)
- Product leadership + PMs using perf as a release signoff input
- Sales Engineering / Solutions (to answer “what’s the baseline, what’s changing, how do we talk about it internally”)

This ticket is not about marketing benchmarks; it’s an internal baseline + policy artifact used to standardize release signoff and avoid recurring debates about “what is the metric / what is noise / what is a regression”.

## Deliverable(s)
1) **Confluence page**: “Q1 2026 Serving Runtime Performance Baseline (Internal)”
   - Location proposal: `sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/q1-2026-perf-baseline-plan.json` (plan) + new page for the finalized baseline report (PM to create in Confluence, link back to plan)
2) **Google Doc / PDF export** for leadership circulation (same content as Confluence, but stable snapshot)
3) **One-page summary** section at top (exec-readable)
4) **Release gating policy section** (what gates, where, thresholds, exceptions, escalation)

## Inputs / References (expected to link from report)
- Methodology + success criteria: `sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/q1-2026-perf-baseline-plan.json`
- Workload suite definition v1: `sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/representative-workload-suite-v1.json`
- Measurement & manifest schema: `sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0172-benchmark-metrics-and-run-manifest-format.json`
- Workload sourcing + privacy constraints: `sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0173-representative-workload-sourcing-from-prod-telemetry.json`
- Regression policy + thresholds: `sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/perf-regression-policy-and-thresholds.json`
- SLO alignment guidance: `sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/latency-slo-alignment-for-perf-baselines.json`
- Dashboard spec: `sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/perf-baseline-dashboards-spec.json`
- Drive tracker (baseline runs): `sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/q1-2026-baseline-run-tracker.json`
- Drive notes (open questions / variance): `sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/q1-2026-perf-baseline-notes-wip.json`
- Gating proposal draft: `sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/perf-suite-release-gating-proposal.json`

## Scope of the report (what it must include)
### A) Executive summary (top of doc)
- What we benchmarked (models, HW, regions, workloads)
- What the baseline represents (anchor build/tag + baseline freeze date)
- High-level baseline “headline” numbers (not exhaustive) + major caveats
- What’s gated now vs later (phased rollout of gating)
- Top risks + mitigations (variance sources, fleet capacity, kernel fallback instability)

### B) Baseline definition
Must explicitly state:
- **Baseline anchor**: runtime build/tag, container image digest (if applicable), CUDA/driver versions, kernel selection mode, scheduler policy baseline
- **Regions**: at minimum us-east + eu-west (and any caveats for fleet parity)
- **Hardware SKUs**: H100 / A100 / L40S where applicable (list what’s fully covered vs partial)
- **Models**: top deployed families (Llama / Qwen / Mistral variants) — enumerate exact model IDs and quantization profiles included
- **Workloads** (representative suite v1):
  - Chat streaming (short prompts, variable decode)
  - Long-context summarization (large prefill, modest decode)
  - Tool/function calling (bursty multi-turn)
  - Embeddings (high-QPS, small payload)
- **Cache scenarios**: report both **cold** and **warm** (prefix/KV caching) where meaningful; explain what “warm” means in the harness and what it does not mean (no prompt content retention; seeded synthetic prompts; cache priming described)

### C) Canonical metrics + definitions (must align to ADR-0172)
The report must define the metric boundaries used in the baseline tables:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token / first-token-on-wire for streaming) and what is excluded (client read / downstream proxy overhead)
- TPOT (time per output token) and whether it is computed server-side; clarify if it excludes network time
- Throughput (tokens/s or req/s) by workload type
- Percentiles: p50 / p95 / p99 where available, with a short note on tail-latency importance and how we attribute tails (queueing vs kernel vs KV pressure)

### D) Summary tables (the “meat” of the report)
Minimum table set (can be expanded):
1) **Chat streaming baseline**: per model x region x GPU
   - TTFT p50/p95/p99
   - TPOT p50/p95/p99
   - Concurrency target and achieved tokens/s
2) **Long-context prefill**: per model x region x GPU
   - Prefill latency p50/p95/p99 (or TTFT if that’s the chosen proxy)
   - Queue wait contribution (if available) and notable scheduling settings
3) **Tool/function calling**: multi-turn burst behavior
   - p95 TTFT under burst + sustained
   - any load-shed / backpressure counters (qualitative summary if not stable enough for a numeric target)
4) **Embeddings**: req/s + latency percentiles
   - req/s at steady QPS targets
   - p95/p99 latency

For each table: include a “notes” column capturing important configuration: scheduler policy ID, kernel selection mode/pinning, cache scenario.

### E) Noise model and what counts as regression
This section needs to be explicit and non-negotiable (link to the company standard):
- Sample sizes used for baseline (and why)
- Expected run-to-run variance bands by workload / SKU (even if rough)
- Definition of “regression” vs “noise” used for gating
- What we do when an alert triggers (triage loop, rerun checklist, escalation)

### F) Release gating policy (internal)
We need an opinionated policy that connects baseline metrics to release signoff.
- Where gating runs:
  - PR-level: limited subset (smoke perf checks; non-blocking initially or blocking for narrow metrics)
  - Nightly: full representative suite on benchmark fleet
  - Release branch: gating mode (blocking) with explicit overrides
- What blocks a release:
  - Examples: p95 TTFT regression above threshold on “golden” workload(s) for top 2 models on H100 in us-east
  - Define what is informational only (e.g., A100/L40S partial coverage) vs hard gate
- Exceptions:
  - Allowed override roles (Runtime TL / SRE TL + PM approval)
  - Required documentation: link to manifest + rerun + known issue + follow-up issue key
- Communications:
  - Alert routing to `#eng-runtime` and `#eng-sre` triage channels
  - When to page (almost never) vs when to notify (most cases)

## Proposed outline (for the Confluence page)
1. TL;DR / Executive summary
2. Baseline scope (models, hardware, regions)
3. Representative workload suite v1 (taxonomy + mapping to prod cohorts)
4. Methodology (measurement boundaries + manifest)
5. Results: summary tables + key takeaways
6. Regression policy and noise model
7. Release gating policy (what gates where)
8. Appendix: run manifests, dashboard links, known cliffs, open issues

## Acceptance criteria
- A single Confluence page exists and is linked from the ENG umbrella ticket (ENG-4821) and the perf regression policy doc.
- Includes at least the 4 summary tables listed above, with clear legends and configuration notes.
- Explicitly states baseline anchor build + freeze date, and cache scenarios reported.
- Includes a “gating policy” section that Connor O’Brien (release gating) and Sean Gallagher (SRE) sign off on.
- Exec sponsors (Neha Kapoor, Dr. Maya Srinivasan) receive the doc link + 1-page summary, and provide “looks good” feedback or tracked edits.

## Owners / reviewers
- DRI (PM): Marissa Cole
- Reviewers:
  - Mateo Alvarez (runtime lead): accuracy of baseline + takeaways
  - Rina Kobayashi / Claire Dubois: methodology correctness
  - Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant: gating + metrics alignment
  - Jonas Weber / Dr. Maya Srinivasan: workload representativeness and quality guardrails language

## Open questions (need answers before final publish)
1) What exact runtime tag/build is the Q1 baseline anchor? (see `#eng-runtime` thread about freeze date)
2) For TTFT definition, are we using “first token emitted by server” or “first token flushed to socket”? (ensure we match ADR + harness)
3) Which model variants are considered “top deployed” for gating purposes (top 2? top 5?) and by which cohort (hosted vs dedicated)?
4) For warm-cache, are we reporting “cache primed within the same process” only, or do we have a stable way to represent cross-run cache behavior?

## Non-goals
- External publication or competitive comparison
- Single-number claims like “X% faster than Y”
- Re-litigating the representative workload suite definition (we can note v2 backlog items, but v1 is what we publish)

2026-01-14 (Claire Dubois): Please make sure we include the metric boundary callouts (TTFT/TPOT) up front. We’ve had repeated confusion in reviews about client overhead vs server time; ADR-0172 has the canonical wording.

2026-01-18 (Sean Gallagher): For gating policy, let’s be explicit about what’s a hard gate vs informational. On-call should not get paged for benchmark variance; routing should be triage channel + a Jira/Linear follow-up if persistent.

2026-01-22 (Mateo Alvarez): Baseline anchor likely runtime-1.20.3, but we’re waiting on the kernel pin decision for L40S. OK to publish with a note that L40S is ‘partial coverage’ and not used for hard gating in v1.

2026-02-03 (Connor O’Brien): Gating language should mention override requirements. We’ve had release managers ask ‘who can push past perf gates’—need a simple rule: Runtime TL + SRE TL approval + follow-up ticket link.

2026-02-11 (Jonas Weber): Add a brief paragraph on quality guardrails: perf improvements must not silently change decoding/quality. Link to the lightweight spot-check hook and state that it’s non-blocking but required for release signoff on major runtime changes.

2026-02-18 (Neha Kapoor): Exec summary should include: what’s new since last quarter, top 2 risks (variance + fleet capacity), and what decision we need from leadership (continued GPU-hours allocation + enforce gating on release branches).
